plain_description.what: No calls. Using 21 trees built with different random seeds (plus 3 trees of the newer recipe), the test measured how much each leaf changes between consecutive rebuilds when only the seed and the data split change. It also measured a pure-chance floor.
plain_description.why: It sets a baseline for how much a leaf 'moves' by chance alone, so a later rule for re-opening a cell after a rebuild is not triggered by noise.
plain_description.information: It shows what a re-opening threshold would flag under pure noise. Result: undetermined by design (a readout with no pass/fail criterion). Leaves overlap with their successor at a median of 0.57 to 0.67. A 0.66 per-leaf bar would re-open about half or more of the leaves from a seed change alone. The '0.66-0.69' figure quoted earlier holds for whole-tree agreement, not per leaf. The effect of a real growth step (adding data) was not measured.
